$comment: This repository's own load-bearing rules, as entries with a predicate. Rendered by scripts/invariant_map.py into INVARIANTS.md; do not edit that file. An entry with neither a checker nor a stated `unenforceable` reason is itself a violation — see the module docstring in scripts/invariants.py for why a rule you cannot check is a rule you do not have.

invariants.rule: Money is int pico-dollars (1e-12 USD). Never introduce a float currency path.
invariants.paid_for: obs/trace.py recorded float(span.cost.picos) into a float64 counter; exact only below 2**53 picos = $9,007.20, on a CUMULATIVE metric
invariants.note: Micro-dollars round cheap-model tokens to zero, so a router that saves money reports saving nothing. The same rounding erases a half-micro-dollar tool called a thousand times.

invariants.rule: Time comes from an injected Clock. Nothing calls datetime.now() or time.monotonic() directly.
invariants.paid_for: guard/sandbox.py read time.monotonic() three times, so duration_seconds was unmockable and no test ever asserted on the field

allowlist.reason: Runner.run(now="") is the injection point and the suite uses it; the default only stamps a report timestamp, which nothing branches on.
age_days(today=None) and is_stale(today=None) take the date; the catalogue is a value object and threading a Clock through it would be heavier than the parameter it already has.

invariants.note: The allowlist is the number to watch. Two entries that each name a working injection point is a boundary; five entries with vague reasons is a rule that has quietly stopped applying.

invariants.rule: Any StrEnum compared with < or > must define all four comparison operators explicitly.
invariants.paid_for: factory.Stage — inherited string comparison makes Stage.DEPLOY < Stage.IDEA true, and @total_ordering fills in nothing because all four operators are already inherited
invariants.note: The failure is silent and confident: a pipeline ordered by inherited string comparison permits every backwards move whose stage name happens to sort earlier, and the check still reads as working.

invariants.rule: Symbol resolution lives in omnex.core.symbols and is imported, never copied.
invariants.paid_for: ontology_map.py, node_map.py and omnex.factory were about to hold three copies of one four-line check
invariants.note: The splitter is what a second copy costs: a quadratic fixed in the engine survived in citegate for a further commit.

invariants.rule: The sentence splitter exists twice on purpose; the two copies must behave identically.
invariants.paid_for: the abbreviation sets diverged by dr./mr./ms. while the two FUNCTIONS stayed line-for-line identical, so citegate split "Mr. Lee and Ms. Park disagreed." into four fragments
invariants.note: citegate ships dependency-free and may not import the engine, so the duplication stays. What changes is that a convention held it before and a check holds it now.

invariants.rule: engine/pyproject.toml declares no runtime dependency; heavy libraries sit behind Protocol adapters as optional extras.
invariants.paid_for: stated in CLAUDE.md since the first commit and never verified by anything
invariants.note: This is what makes the suite runnable on a bare interpreter, which is in turn why it gets run. The first required dependency is the one that quietly ends that.

invariants.rule: A stated limitation is kept as a passing test rather than a paragraph.
invariants.paid_for: test_a_paraphrase_outside_the_corpus_is_missed and the inverted-polarity grounding test are supposed to be green
invariants.unenforceable: Whether a green test is an honesty anchor or an ordinary assertion is a judgement about intent, and a checker keying on names would be satisfied by renaming a test.
invariants.note: Enforced socially and by review. Listed here so the count of unenforceable rules is visible rather than absent.

invariants.rule: A refusal names every failing condition at once, not the first.
invariants.paid_for: worth_it.raise_if_not_worth_it and AgentSpec.audit both collect rather than short-circuit
invariants.unenforceable: Requires knowing that a function is a refusal and that its checks are independent. Every mechanical proxy — counting raises, looking for early returns — flags correct code and misses the real cases.
invariants.note: Being refused repeatedly is how somebody concludes the check is the obstacle.

invariants.rule: Docstrings explain why, and name the failure the code prevents.
invariants.paid_for: the convention this whole codebase is written in
invariants.unenforceable: A length or keyword check would be satisfied by padding, which is worse than no check: it converts a real convention into a quota.
invariants.note: Goodhart. A metric for prose quality is a metric for prose volume.

invariants.rule: A listing that is live may not promise more images than QC has passed.
invariants.paid_for: the EUR49 Complete Vault sells "170+ images" while the four QC manifests total 80 — a 90-image shortfall a buyer would discover after paying
invariants.note: Scoped to LIVE offers on purpose. "You must have 170 images" would be red until the day they exist, and a permanently red build is one people learn to ignore — the exact failure this registry was built against. `live` mirrors registry.ts's `enabled`: nothing sells today, so nothing is violated today, and the gate bites the moment somebody publishes. packs/listing_check.py reports the shortfall for every offer regardless, live or not.
